Topic 3.3: Mass, Volume, Weight and Density
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mass, Volume, Weight and Density, part of Measurements 3.2 Volume of Solids (8 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand the  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you weigh materials and objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs different instruments and tools used in weighing materials or objects and relate to consumer awareness and protection. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs different instruments and tools used in weighing materials or objects and relate to consumer awareness and protection. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication-aac (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mass, Volume, Weight and Density together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration – as the learner discusses the relationship between mass and weight.

● Creativity and imagination – as the learner determines the density of different materials or objects.

● Digital literacy – as the learner uses IT devices to determine the mass, volume and density of different objects.

33

Values:
● Integrity – as the learner gives correct masses and weights of different material and objects.

● Responsibility – as the learner works and take care of weighing machines and other resources.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) - Careers in business such as shop keeping where weighing tools are used.

● Self-awareness – as the learner weighs themselves for health purposes.

Link to other subjects:

Integrated Science – as the learner uses machines and tools which involve weighing and balancing.
